definition_zh: 教练；训练师；训练器；运动鞋（英式口语）
definition_en: a person or device that trains others, or (British) a sports shoe
core_image: 站在场边掐秒表的人：把零散动作串成规定动作的人
scene: 体育馆里哨声一响，教练挥手让队员们开始折返跑： The whistle blew in the gym, and the coach waved the team to start shuttle runs under the trainer.
sceneCN: 这里 trainer 是「教练」（第 1 个义项：指导训练的人）；句意是教练哨响后带队折返跑。

pos.zh: 训练器；运动鞋（英式口语）

derivatives.zh: 由 trainee 加 -ship 构成，义为「培训期；见习岗位」

同根词「训练；培训」，由 train 加现在分词构成

senses.title: A person who coaches people or animals
senses.definition: a person who teaches skills or prepares people and animals for performance
senses.definitionCN: 教授技能或训练人、动物以达成绩效的人
senses.example: The trainer made the team run ten laps before lunch.
senses.exampleCN: 教练让全队午饭前跑了十圈。
senses.why: The core image is the one who keeps the line of practice moving.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是让那串「练习车厢」持续前进的人。

senses.title: A device used for practice
senses.definition: a machine or simulator used for practice or exercise
senses.definitionCN: 用于练习或锻炼的器械或模拟装置
senses.example: Pilots practise landings in a flight trainer.
senses.exampleCN: 飞行员在飞行训练器上练习着陆。
senses.why: The device stands in for the coach, guiding the same repeated drill.
senses.whyCN: 器械替代教练，引导同样的重复操练。

senses.title: A sports shoe (British informal)
senses.definition: a soft shoe worn for sport or casual wear in British English
senses.definitionCN: 英式英语中用于运动或休闲的软底鞋
senses.example: He bought new white trainers for the gym.
senses.exampleCN: 他为健身买了新的白色运动鞋。
senses.why: Shoes worn while training took the trainer's name.
senses.whyCN: 训练时穿的鞋，便借了 trainer 的名号。

intro.en: Trainer is the agent noun of train, built with the native -er suffix. The shoe sense arose in British English because such shoes were worn for training.
intro.cn: trainer 是动词 train 加本土施动后缀 -er 构成的施动名词。「运动鞋」义产生于英式英语，因这种鞋在训练时穿着而得名。

items.en: Latin trahere, to pull, underlies the family through Old French train.
items.cn: 拉丁语 trahere（拉）经古法语 train 支撑整个词族。

items.en: train meant to pull or trail along.
items.cn: 古法语 train 意为「拉、拖曳」。

items.en: Trainer first named one who draws up or educates; also one who treats disease by diet and exercise.
items.cn: 16 世纪 trainer 指「教育者」，也指以饮食运动治病的人。

items.en: The sports coach sense became dominant with modern athletics.
items.cn: 随着现代体育兴起，教练义占主导。

items.en: British informal use extended to sports shoes; American English prefers sneakers.
items.cn: 20 世纪英式口语把该词用于运动鞋，美式则说 sneakers。

note.en: Words that look or sound close to trainer, and words in the coaching field.
note.cn: 与 trainer 形近音近的词，以及同属教练义场的词。

definition_zh: 必然地；必定；不可避免地；不一定（用于 not necessarily）
definition_en: in a way that cannot be avoided or that follows with logical certainty; also used in the phrase not necessarily to deny that something is always true
core_image: 一条被两端拉紧的锁链，中间没有可以退让的余地
scene: 山道上的碎石还湿着，跑得太急的人收不住脚，一定会摔下去。 If you run down a wet slope, you will necessarily fall.
sceneCN: 这里「necessarily」是「必然地、必定」（第 1 个义项：由逻辑或事实逼出来的结果）；句意是跑下湿滑斜坡的人必然会摔倒。图中可辨识物件：湿漉漉的碎石、斜坡、收不住的脚步。

pos.zh: 必然地；必定；不可避免地

derivatives.zh: 与 necessarily 同出于拉丁 necessarius，义为「必要的；必然的」
由拉丁 necessitas 进入英语，义为「必要性；必然性」
由 necessity 加动词后缀 -ate 构成，义为「使成为必要」

senses.title: As a logical certainty
senses.definition: in a way that follows by logic, so that no other result is possible
senses.definitionCN: 按逻辑推演下来必然如此，不可能有别的结果
senses.example: A triangle necessarily has three sides.
senses.exampleCN: 三角形必然有三条边。
senses.why: Latin necesse joined ne, not, with cedere, to give way: what cannot give way cannot be escaped, so the adverb states a result that logic or fact forces.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 necesse 把「不」与「退让」拼在一起：不肯退让的东西就躲不开，所以这个副词说的是逻辑或事实逼出来的结果。

senses.title: In every case, without exception
senses.titleCN: 不可避免地；每次都如此
senses.definition: in a way that happens in all cases, because the circumstances leave no room for an alternative
senses.definitionCN: 在所有情形下都会发生，因为客观条件没有留下别的可能
senses.example: When demand outruns supply, prices necessarily rise.
senses.exampleCN: 当需求超过供给，价格必然上涨。
senses.why: The same picture of a chain with no slack moves from one deduction to a general rule: once the conditions hold, the outcome cannot be held back.
senses.whyCN: 同一幅「锁链没有余量」的画面，从单次推论扩展到普遍规律：条件一旦成立，结果就压不住。

senses.title: Not in every case, in the phrase not necessarily
senses.definition: used after not to say that something is possible but not always or not certainly true
senses.definitionCN: 用在 not 之后，表示某事有可能，但并非总是或并非一定成立
senses.example: A quiet student is not necessarily a bored one.
senses.exampleCN: 安静的学生不一定就是觉得无聊。
senses.why: Negating a word of absolute certainty leaves a deliberate gap: the link may hold sometimes, but it is not forced, so the phrase warns against a hasty conclusion.
senses.whyCN: 把表示绝对必然的词一否定，就留下一个刻意的空隙：这种联系有时成立，却不是被逼出来的，所以这个说法是在提醒人别急着下结论。

intro.en: Necessarily is the adverb built on necessary, and the two words share one Latin idea: a necessity that cannot be pushed aside.
intro.cn: necessarily 是由 necessary 加 -ly 构成的副词，两词共享同一个拉丁观念：一种推不开的必然。

items.en: A negative particle and a root for yielding are generally reconstructed behind the Latin family, though the exact earlier shape is debated.
items.cn: 一般认为拉丁语这一族词的背后有一个否定小词和一个表示「退让」的词根，但更早的具体形式仍有争议。

items.en: Latin necesse meant unavoidable or inevitable; a common account reads it as ne, not, plus cedere, to give way.
items.cn: 拉丁语 necesse 意为不可避免、必然；一种常见解释是 ne（不）加 cedere（退让）。

items.en: The adjective necessarius described what one cannot do without, carrying the idea of an unyielding necessity into everyday need.
items.cn: 形容词 necessarius 描述离不开的东西，把「不肯退让的必然」带进了日常的「需要」。

items.en: Middle English used necessarie for what must be, and the adverb grew beside it with the ending -ly.
items.cn: 中古英语用 necessarie 表示「必须如此的」，副词形式随后加 -ly 长出来。

items.en: Modern English keeps necessarily for logical and practical certainty, and the negative phrase not necessarily for the deliberate exception.
items.cn: 现代英语保留 necessarily 表示逻辑与事实上的确定，并用否定短语 not necessarily 表示刻意留下的例外。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin family and its English endings; the near-meaning group gathers adverbs of certainty and of unavoidable occurrence.
note.cn: 形近组沿着拉丁词族与英语词尾展开；近义组收表示确定与不可避免发生的副词。

entries.definition: The adjective behind the adverb, meaning needed or certain.
entries.definitionCN: 副词背后的形容词，义为「必要的；必然的」。

entries.definition: The state or quality of being necessary.
entries.definitionCN: 必要性；必然性。

entries.definition: To make something necessary.
entries.definitionCN: 使某事成为必要。

entries.definition: In a way that is not needed.
entries.definitionCN: 以不必要的方式。

entries.definition: In a way that cannot be prevented.
entries.definitionCN: 不可避免地；终究会。

entries.definition: In a way that cannot be escaped.
entries.definitionCN: 无法避免地。

entries.definition: Without doubt; for sure.
entries.definitionCN: 无疑地；肯定地。

normalIntro.en: The word carries a Latin refusal to budge, and its family keeps turning that refusal into logical certainty and practical necessity.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词带着拉丁语「不肯让步」的劲头，同族词不断把这种不肯让步变成逻辑上的确定与现实中的必需。

normal.en: Necesse is read as ne plus cedere, so the core picture is something that will not give way.
normal.cn: necesse 可拆成 ne 加 cedere，核心画面就是一件不肯退让的东西。

normal.en: The suffix -ly turns the adjective necessary into the adverb necessarily, just as it turns quick into quickly.
normal.cn: -ly 把形容词 necessary 变成副词 necessarily，就像把 quick 变成 quickly。

normal.en: Not necessarily does not cancel the word; it denies that the link holds in every case.
normal.cn: not necessarily 并没有取消这个词，它否认的是这种联系在每种情况下都成立。

normal.en: Necessity and necessitate are relatives: one names the state, the other the act of making something necessary.
normal.cn: necessity 与 necessitate 是同族词：一个指状态，一个指使某事成为必要的动作。

normal.en: In a proof, necessarily marks the step that no counterexample can overturn.
normal.cn: 在证明里，necessarily 标出的是任何反例都推不翻的那一步。

abstract.en: A chain tightened at both ends is a good picture of a conclusion that cannot be loosened by argument.
abstract.cn: 两端拉紧的锁链，很适合形容一个怎么争辩都松不开的结论。

abstract.en: The negative phrase works like a small door left open in an otherwise closed wall.
abstract.cn: 那个否定短语就像一堵封闭的墙上故意留下的一扇小门。

abstract.en: Every time the word appears, someone is claiming that the room for choice has shrunk to nothing.
abstract.cn: 这个词每次出现，都有人在声称可供选择的空间已经缩到没有。

examples.en: A triangle necessarily has three sides.
examples.cn: 三角形必然有三条边。

examples.en: When demand outruns supply, prices necessarily rise.
examples.cn: 当需求超过供给，价格必然上涨。

examples.en: A quiet student is not necessarily a bored one.
examples.cn: 安静的学生不一定就是觉得无聊。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「呢色塞热利」——听着像一串含糊的尾音，意思却是躲不开的必然；记住 necessarily 是必然地。

root: 拉丁语 necesse（不可避免）一般认为由否定成分 ne- 与 cedere（退让）构成；加 -arius 得 necessarius，再加 -ly 成为 necessarily。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a necessity that will not yield; the senses divide into logical certainty, universal occurrence, and the negated phrase that keeps one exception alive.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一种不肯退让的必然；义项分出逻辑上的确定、普遍发生的情形，以及保留一个例外的否定说法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a chain pulled tight at both ends, with no slack left in the middle.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条两端拉紧的锁链，中间不留一点余量。

branches.en: a proof that closes every other door one by one
branches.cn: 证明把其他可能的门一扇扇关掉

branches.en: three sides that cannot be counted otherwise
branches.cn: 三条边怎么数都改不了

branches.en: a price climbing because supply has run short
branches.cn: 供给短缺，价格随之上抬

branches.en: a calm face read as boredom without proof
branches.cn: 凭一张平静的脸就断定人家无聊

branches.en: a question answered with a careful maybe
branches.cn: 一个问题只得到谨慎的「也许」

intro.en: One Latin adjective of necessity, its negative and verbal parts, and two English endings hold this entry together.
intro.cn: 一个表示必然的拉丁形容词、它的否定与动词成分，以及两个英语词尾共同撑起这个词条。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies the whole family: necesse, its adjective necessarius and the verb cedere behind the negative element.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了整族词：necesse、它的形容词 necessarius，以及藏在否定成分背后的动词 cedere。

definition_zh: 记者；新闻工作者
definition_en: a person who writes news stories or reports events for a newspaper, magazine, or broadcast service
core_image: 一个人抱着本子挤在人群最前面，边问边记
scene: 雨里围着警戒线，几个人举着手机和录音笔追问路人。 A journalist asked the same question three different ways.
sceneCN: 这里 journalist 是「记者」（第 1 个义项：为媒体采写报道的人），句意为一位记者把同一个问题换着问了三种说法。画面里的物件：录音笔、本子、警戒线。

derivatives.zh: 由本词词干加 -ism 构成，义为「新闻业」
由本词词干加 -ic 构成，义为「新闻的」
由词根直接构成，义为「期刊；日记」
同源于 jour「日」的形近词，义为「旅程」

senses.title: Reporter for the news
senses.definition: a person whose job is to gather facts and write or broadcast the news
senses.definitionCN: 以收集事实并写成或播出新闻为职业的人
senses.example: A journalist from the local paper rang to check the date.
senses.exampleCN: 当地报纸的一位记者打电话来核对日期。
senses.why: The word grew out of journal, a daily record, so a journalist is literally a day-writer.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由 journal「每日记录」长出来，字面上就是「写日子的人」。

senses.title: Writer of opinion and features
senses.definition: a person who writes longer pieces, comment, or interviews for a publication
senses.definitionCN: 为刊物撰写长文、评论或访谈的人
senses.example: She works as a journalist for a monthly science magazine.
senses.exampleCN: 她在一家科学月刊做撰稿人。
senses.why: As papers grew, the job widened from daily reports to any written news work.
senses.whyCN: 随着报纸增多，这个职业从每日报道扩展到各种文字新闻工作。

intro.en: Journalist is journal, "a daily record", plus -ist; its root is the Latin word for day.
intro.cn: journalist 是 journal「每日记录」加 -ist，其词根是拉丁语的「日」。

items.en: dies meant "day".
items.cn: dies 意为「日」。

items.en: diurnalis meant "daily".
items.cn: diurnalis 意为「每日的」。

items.en: jour kept the day sense; journal named a daily book.
items.cn: jour 保留「日」，journal 指每日的记录簿。

items.en: English used journal for a daily paper.
items.cn: 英语用 journal 指日报。

items.en: The -ist ending marked the person who wrote for it.
items.cn: -ist 词尾标出为它写作的人。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the journ- stem; the near-meaning group holds news jobs by medium.
note.cn: 形近组共用 journ- 词干；近义组按媒介区分新闻行当。

entries.definition: The work or industry of news reporting.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「新闻业」，同词干。

entries.definition: A trip from one place to another.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「旅程」，同「日」词根。

entries.definition: Typical of news reporting.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「新闻式的」，同词干。

entries.definition: One who gathers and reports news.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「记者」，偏出镜与现场。

entries.definition: A reporter based in a particular place.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「驻外记者」，强调常驻。

entries.definition: One who prepares and approves copy.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「编辑」，对稿件加工。

normalIntro.en: These hooks keep the day in the middle of the word.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把「日」留在词的正中间。

normal.en: French jour means day.
normal.cn: 法语 jour 就是「日」。

normal.en: A journal is a book written by the day.
normal.cn: journal 是逐日写下的本子。

normal.en: A journalist writes for the daily.
normal.cn: journalist 就是给日报写东西的人。

normal.en: -ist marks the person, -ism marks the trade.
normal.cn: -ist 指人，-ism 指这一行。

normal.en: Journalism is what the journalist does.
normal.cn: journalism 是 journalist 所做的事。

abstract.en: A journalist is a witness who files copy.
abstract.cn: 记者是交稿的目击者。

abstract.en: The day is the unit; the story is the product.
abstract.cn: 单位是日，产品是故事。

abstract.en: A good reporter asks boring questions until something breaks.
abstract.cn: 好记者一直问无聊的问题，直到有东西裂开。

examples.en: The journalist spent a week on the same street.
examples.cn: 这位记者在同一条街上待了一周。

examples.en: Two journalists were refused entry to the meeting.
examples.cn: 两名记者被拒绝进入会场。

examples.en: She moved from local radio to print journalism.
examples.cn: 她当地电台转做纸质新闻。

dict_mnemonic.text: journal（日报）+ ist（人）——给日报写字的人

root: 拉丁语 dies「日」→ diurnalis「每日的」→ 古法语 journal「每日记录」→ 英语 journal + -ist → journalist。同族有 journalism、journalistic、journey。

sensesIntro.en: Two senses: a news reporter, and a writer of longer pieces or columns.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项：采写新闻的记者，以及撰写长文或专栏的撰稿人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: someone standing at the front of a crowd, asking and writing.
core.cn: 核心意象：挤在人群最前面、边问边写的人。

branches.en: THE NOTEBOOK: notes taken in the street.
branches.cn: 本子这条线：在街上记下的字。

branches.en: THE COLUMN: longer pieces written at a desk.
branches.cn: 专栏这条线：在书桌前写成的长文。

branches.en: THE DEADLINE: both senses live by the daily clock.
branches.cn: 截稿这条线：两个义项都跟着日内的钟走。

branches.en: THE SOURCE: both senses depend on someone who talked.
branches.cn: 消息源这条线：两个义项都要有人开口。

branches.en: THE CLOCK: writing is measured in days, not hours.
branches.cn: 时钟这条线：写稿是按天算，不按小时算。

intro.en: Journalist is journ- "day" plus -al and the person-ending -ist.
intro.cn: journalist 是 journ-「日」加 -al，再加指人的 -ist。

latinIntro.en: Latin dies and diurnalis are both recorded.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 dies 与 diurnalis 均有记载。

items.example: The root also appears in journey.
It forms journal, a daily book.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 journal，每日的本子。

definition_zh: 个人的；单独的；独特的；个人；个体
definition_en: relating to one single person or thing, separate and distinct, or a single human being considered on their own
core_image: 一件不能再被切开的东西：切到它这里就到底了
scene: 球场边，教练挨个点名叫队员出列，目光在每个人身上停留片刻。 The coach praised every individual on the team for trying his best.
sceneCN: 这里 individual 是「个人、个体」（第 4 个义项：作为单个人来看的人）；句意：队里每一个个人都必须了解计划，不只是队长。图中可辨识物件：战术板、逐个点名的手指、球员。

pos.zh: 个人的；单独的；独特的；单个的
个人；个体；单个人或事物

collocations.zh: 私人（普通个人，非官方身份）

forms.label: 比较级（更多用 more 构成）
最高级（更多用 most 构成）

senses.title: Single and separate
senses.titleCN: 单独的：作为一个单位分开看
senses.definition: relating to one single person or thing, considered separately from the group
senses.definitionCN: 指单个的人或物，从群体中分开来看
senses.example: Each individual case must be judged on its own facts.
senses.exampleCN: 每个单独的案件都必须依其自身事实判断。
senses.why: Latin individuus is in- 'not' + dividuus 'divisible'. An individual is the point at which division stops, so the first sense is simply 'one that cannot be split further'.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 individuus 由 in-“不”+ dividuus“可分的”构成。individual 就是“分割停止的那一点”，因此第一个义项就是“无法再被切开的一个”。

senses.title: Distinctive and personal
senses.titleCN: 独特的：带有个人印记的
senses.definition: having a quality or style that is clearly one's own and different from others
senses.definitionCN: 具有明显属于自己、区别于他人的品质或风格
senses.example: The room has an individual character that no catalogue could copy.
senses.exampleCN: 这个房间有一种目录册无法复制的独特气质。
senses.why: Once a thing is separated from the group, its differences become visible. The word moves from 'single' to 'uniquely marked'.
senses.whyCN: 一旦某物从群体中分开，它的差异就变得可见。这个词于是从“单个”转为“带有独特标记”。

senses.title: Intended for one person
senses.titleCN: 供一人用的：按个人配置
senses.definition: designed or intended for one person rather than for a group
senses.definitionCN: 为一个人而非一群人所设计或准备的
senses.example: The airline serves individual portions of ice cream.
senses.exampleCN: 航空公司提供单人份的冰淇淋。
senses.why: This sense is recorded from 1889. The unit of distribution becomes one person, so the portion is cut to the size of an individual.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项自 1889 年有记录。分配单位变成了一个人，于是份额被切到“个体”的大小。

senses.title: A single human being
senses.titleCN: 个人：作为单个人来看的人
senses.definition: one human being, especially when considered apart from a group or society
senses.definitionCN: 一个人，尤指与群体或社会分开来看时
senses.example: The law protects the individual as well as the community.
senses.exampleCN: 法律既保护个人，也保护社群。
senses.why: The noun sense, recorded from the 1640s, applies the 'indivisible unit' idea to a person. Each person is a unit that cannot be dissolved into the crowd.
senses.whyCN: 名词义自 17 世纪 40 年代有记录，把“不可分的单位”这一观念用到了人身上。每个人都是无法被溶解进人群的单位。

senses.title: A biological individual
senses.titleCN: 生物个体：一个独立的生命单位
senses.definition: in biology, a single organism considered as a distinct unit
senses.definitionCN: 生物学中，作为独立单位看待的单个生物体
senses.example: The study tracked one hundred individual birds.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究追踪了一百只单独的鸟。
senses.why: Biology needs a countable unit below the species and above the cell. The individual is that unit: one life that can be observed and counted.
senses.whyCN: 生物学需要一个低于物种、高于细胞的计数单位。individual 就是那个单位：一条可被观察与计数的生命。

senses.title: Informal: a person of a certain kind
senses.titleCN: （口语）某个家伙：带评价色彩的人
senses.definition: in colloquial use, a person, often with mildly negative or ironic judgement
senses.definitionCN: 口语用法中指一个人，常带轻微贬义或讽刺评价
senses.example: A rather odd individual was asking about you.
senses.exampleCN: 有个挺奇怪的家伙在打听你。
senses.why: The colloquial 'person' sense is attested from 1742. Calling someone 'an individual' distances them, as if viewing them as a specimen rather than a person.
senses.whyCN: 口语“人”义自 1742 年有记录。把某人称作 an individual 会产生距离感，仿佛把他当作标本而不是人来看。

senses.title: Relating to one member's rights
senses.definition: relating to the rights, duties, or liberties of one person rather than a collective
senses.definitionCN: 指一个人的权利、义务或自由，而非集体的
senses.example: Individual rights must be balanced against public safety.
senses.exampleCN: 个人权利必须与公共安全相权衡。
senses.why: Political thought uses the word to mark the boundary between the person and the collective. The indivisible unit is also the unit that holds rights.
senses.whyCN: 政治思想用这个词标记个人与集体之间的边界。那个不可分的单位，也是持有权利的单位。

senses.title: An indivisible particle
senses.titleCN: 不可分的单元：原子式的个体
senses.definition: in older philosophy, an indivisible entity or atom
senses.definitionCN: 较旧哲学中，一个不可分的实体或原子
senses.example: The old philosophers argued that every body is made of individuals.
senses.exampleCN: 古代哲学家论证说，每个物体都由不可分的单元构成。
senses.why: Latin individuum as a noun meant 'an atom, an indivisible particle'. The atom is the limiting case of the word's literal meaning.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语名词 individuum 意为“原子、不可分的微粒”。原子正是这个词字面意义的极限情形。

senses.title: A distinct entity in a system
senses.definition: one distinct item treated as a unit within a larger system, such as a record or an account
senses.definitionCN: 在更大系统中被当作单位处理的一个独立项目，如一条记录或一个账户
senses.example: Each individual account is audited once a year.
senses.exampleCN: 每个单独的账户每年审计一次。
senses.why: The unit idea travels beyond people. Any system that must keep parts separate marks each one as an individual, whether it is a person, a record, or a cell.
senses.whyCN: “单位”观念可以走出人。任何必须把部分保持分开的系统，都会把每一项标记为 individual，不论是人、记录还是细胞。

intro.en: Individual is the negative of divisible: Latin in- 'not' + dividere 'divide'. Its first English use was theological, about the indivisible Trinity; the modern 'single person' sense is only about 400 years old.
intro.cn: individual 是 divisible 的否定式：拉丁语 in-“不”+ dividere“分开”。它最早的英语用法是神学的，指不可分的三位一体；现代“单个人”的义项只有约四百年历史。

items.en: First recorded as 'one and indivisible, inseparable', with reference to the Trinity. This original sense is now obsolete.
items.cn: 最早记录为“单一且不可分、不可分离”，用于指三位一体。这一最初义项如今已废弃。

items.en: Individualis was formed from Latin individuus 'indivisible', from in- 'not' + dividuus 'divisible'. The word was rare before c. 1600; the 15c. example may be an outlier.
items.cn: individualis 由拉丁语 individuus“不可分的”构成，后者来自 in-“不”+ dividuus“可分的”。这个词在 1600 年前并不常见；15 世纪的用例可能只是孤例。

items.en: Dividere 'to force apart, cleave, distribute' is dis- 'apart' + -videre 'to separate', from PIE *(d)uid- 'to separate, distinguish'. Individual therefore contains the idea of division by negating it. The roots must not be confused: indicare uses dicare 'proclaim', induce uses ducere 'lead', and individual uses dividere 'divide'.
items.cn: dividere“分开、劈开、分配”由 dis-“分开”+ -videre“分离”构成，来自原始印欧语 *(d)uid-“分开、区分”。因此 individual 是通过否定“分割”而包含分割观念的。这些词根不可混淆：indicate 用 dicare“宣告”，induce 用 ducere“引导”，individual 用 dividere“分开”。

items.en: The sense 'single, separate, of but one person or thing' appears. The word now answers the question 'which one, apart from the rest?'
items.cn: “单个的、分开的、只属于一个人或物的”义项出现。此时这个词回答的是“哪一个，与其余分开来看？”

items.en: The noun means 'a single human being' as opposed to a group. Latin individuum had already meant 'an atom, indivisible particle'.
items.cn: 名词指“单个人”，与群体相对。拉丁语 individuum 早已表示“原子、不可分的微粒”。

items.en: The sense 'intended for one person' is recorded in 1889. Individualism as a social philosophy dates from the mid-19c., and individual rights become a central political phrase.
items.cn: “供一人使用的”义项自 1889 年有记录。作为社会哲学的个人主义始于 19 世纪中期，individual rights 则成为核心政治短语。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the divid- root; the near-meaning group separates 'one unit' from 'one person' and 'unique'.
note.cn: 形近组共享 divid- 词根；近义组区分“一个单位”“一个人”与“独特”。

entries.definition: impossible to divide. It shows the root meaning that individual has largely left behind.
entries.definitionCN: 无法分割的。它显出 individual 已大体遗落的词根本义。

entries.definition: the quality of being a distinct person with a character of one's own.
entries.definitionCN: 作为一个有自身性格的独立个体的性质；个性。

entries.definition: a social outlook that gives the individual priority over the collective.
entries.definitionCN: 把个人置于集体之上的社会观念；个人主义。

entries.definition: one only, not one of a group. It is simpler and does not carry the 'indivisible' idea.
entries.definitionCN: 只有一个，不是群体中的一员。它更简单，不带“不可分”的观念。

entries.definition: existing apart from others. It stresses distance, while individual stresses being a distinct unit.
entries.definitionCN: 与他人分开存在的。它强调距离，而 individual 强调是一个独立单位。

entries.definition: one specific person or thing rather than any other. It stresses selection rather than separateness.
entries.definitionCN: 特定的人或物，而非其他。它强调“选定”，而不是“分离”。

entries.definition: a human being. It is the ordinary word, while individual can sound formal or slightly distancing.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人。它是最普通的词，而 individual 可能显得正式或略带距离感。

normalIntro.en: Real roots and real phrases; the in- here means 'not', not 'into'.
normalIntro.cn: 真实词根与真实短语；这里的 in- 是“不”，不是“进入”。

normal.en: in- 'not' + dividere 'divide': an individual is the unit that cannot be divided further.
normal.cn: in-“不”+ dividere“分开”：individual 就是无法再被分割的单位。

normal.en: divide, division and individual share the same root, but individual negates it.
normal.cn: divide、division、individual 共享同一词根，但 individual 对它作了否定。

normal.en: Individual rights treat each person as a unit that cannot be dissolved into the crowd.
normal.cn: individual rights 把每个人当作无法被溶解进人群的单位。

normal.en: An individual portion is cut to the size of one unit rather than the group.
normal.cn: individual portion 是按“一个单位”而非群体切分的份量。

normal.en: Calling someone an individual instead of a person adds a little distance, as if observing a specimen.
normal.cn: 把某人称作 individual 而不是 person，会加一点距离感，仿佛在观察一个标本。

abstract.en: Picture a loaf that can be sliced until only one crumb is left; the crumb that cannot be halved again is the individual.
abstract.cn: 想象一条面包可以被切片，直到只剩一粒碎屑；那粒无法再对半切的碎屑就是 individual。

abstract.en: Every crowd is an optical illusion: lower your eyes far enough and you see only individuals.
abstract.cn: 每一片人群都是一种错觉：把视线降得足够低，你只会看见一个又一个 individual。

abstract.en: Individuality is the scar left by separation: what makes you one thing also makes you unlike the others.
abstract.cn: individuality 是分离留下的印记：让你成为“一个”的东西，也让你不同于其他。

examples.en: The teacher gives individual attention to each learner.
examples.cn: 老师给每个学习者单独的关照。

examples.en: Each individual has a different reason for joining the course.
examples.cn: 每个人加入这门课的理由都不同。

examples.en: The survey interviews individuals rather than households.
examples.cn: 这项调查采访的是个人，而不是家庭。

dict_mnemonic.text: “硬地微丢”+“啊”——硬在地上微微丢了一块，只剩单个个体 → individual 个人、个体

root: 源自中世纪拉丁语 individualis“不可分的”，来自拉丁语 individuus（in-“不”+ dividere“分开”），核心是“切分到这里就停止的单一单位”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of individual, all built on one unit that cannot be divided further. That unit can be a person, an organism, a record, or an atom.
sensesIntro.cn: individual 的九个义项都建立在同一个“无法再被分割的单位”上。这个单位可以是人、生物体、记录，或原子。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a whole that cannot be cut again without ceasing to be itself.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个整体，再切一刀就不再是它自己。

branches.en: ATOM: the literal limit case, an entity with no possible further division.
branches.cn: 原子：字面上的极限情形，一个无法再分的实体。

branches.en: COUNTABLE UNIT: biology, records and cases each need one unit that can be counted.
branches.cn: 可数单位：生物学、记录与案件都需要一个可计数的单位。

branches.en: THE PERSON: the unit is a human being, and that unit is the bearer of rights.
branches.cn: 人：这个单位是一个人，而这个人正是权利的持有者。

branches.en: ONE-PERSON USE: portions and arrangements are cut to the size of one unit.
branches.cn: 单人使用：份额与安排被切到一个单位的大小。

branches.en: DISTINCTION: separation makes difference visible, for praise or for ironic distance.
branches.cn: 区别：分离让差异可见，既可用于赞赏，也可用于讽刺性的距离。

intro.en: Individual is in- 'not' + divid- 'divide' + -ual. English adds -ity, -ism, -ist, -ize and -ly; the prefix here is privative, not locative.
intro.cn: individual 是 in-“不”+ divid-“分开”+ -ual。英语加 -ity、-ism、-ist、-ize、-ly；这里的前缀是否定性的，不是方位性的。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is dividere 'to divide' and individuus 'indivisible'. Relatives include divide, division, dividend and subdivide.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词族是 dividere“分开”与 individuus“不可分的”。同族词包括 divide、division、dividend、subdivide。

items.meaning: the quality of being a distinct person or thing
items.meaningCN: 个性；个体性（-ity 构成性质名词）
items.example: The school encourages individuality rather than uniformity.
items.exampleCN: 这所学校鼓励个性而非一律。

items.meaning: a belief that the individual takes priority over the group
items.meaningCN: 个人主义；认为个人优先于群体的观念
items.example: Individualism shapes much of the country's law.
items.exampleCN: 个人主义塑造了这个国家的大部分法律。

items.meaning: a person who acts independently or believes in individualism
items.meaningCN: 个人主义者；独立行事的人
items.example: She was an individualist who disliked committees.
items.exampleCN: 她是个不喜欢委员会的个人主义者。

items.meaning: marked by independent or self-directed behaviour
items.meaningCN: 个人主义的；强调独立自主的
items.example: The team culture was too individualistic for joint work.
items.exampleCN: 这种团队文化过于个人主义，不适合协作。

items.meaning: to make personal or suited to one person
items.exampleCN: 这款软件会为每道练习定制内容。

items.meaning: the process of making something personal
items.exampleCN: 治疗的个体化能改善结果。
每个文件都被逐一检查。

items.meaning: to distinguish one thing from others; to become a separate self
items.meaningCN: 使区分；使成为独立个体（心理学术语）
items.example: Children individuate slowly from their parents.
items.exampleCN: 孩子会慢慢从父母那里形成独立自我。

items.meaning: the process of becoming a distinct individual
items.meaningCN: 个体化过程；成为独立个体的过程
items.example: Jung described individuation as a lifelong task.
items.exampleCN: 荣格把个体化描述为一项终身任务。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 不可分的；无法被分割的

definition_zh: 无望的；无可救药的
definition_en: having no hope of success or improvement
core_image: 一根燃尽的火柴，最后一缕烟也散了
scene: 没有水，情况看起来毫无希望。 Without water, the situation looked hopeless.
sceneCN: 这里 hopeless 是「无望的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：没有水，情况看起来毫无希望。

collocations.zh: 无可救药的浪漫主义者

senses.title: Without any hope
senses.definition: having no hope of success or change
senses.definitionCN: 没有成功或改变的可能
senses.example: Without water, the situation looked hopeless.
senses.exampleCN: 没有水，情况看起来毫无希望。
senses.why: This is the main sense for situations.
senses.whyCN: 这是描述局面的主要义项。

senses.title: Very bad at something
senses.definition: extremely bad and unlikely to improve
senses.definitionCN: 非常差，几乎不可能改进
senses.example: He is hopeless at fixing things.
senses.exampleCN: 他对修理东西一窍不通。
senses.why: Informally it can mean simply very bad.
senses.whyCN: 口语中也可只表示很差。

intro.en: Hopeless is hope plus -less, without.
intro.cn: hopeless 是 hope 加 -less（没有……的）构成的。

items.en: Hopian meant to hope.
items.cn: hopian 意为希望。

items.en: Leas meant without.
items.cn: leas 意为没有。

items.en: Hopeles meant without hope.
items.cn: hopeles 意为没有希望。

items.en: Hopeless described bad situations.
items.cn: hopeless 描述无望的局面。

items.en: It also came to mean very bad.
items.cn: 它也引申为非常差。

note.en: Hopeless is compared with look-alike words and with words for despair.
note.cn: 把 hopeless 与形近词以及表示绝望的词作比较。

entries.definition: full of hope
entries.definitionCN: 有希望的

entries.definition: unable to act or be helped
entries.definitionCN: 无助的

entries.definition: without a home
entries.definitionCN: 无家可归的

entries.definition: feeling no hope
entries.definitionCN: 绝望的

entries.definition: useless and pointless
entries.definitionCN: 徒劳的

entries.definition: certain to fail
entries.definitionCN: 注定失败的

normalIntro.en: Hopeless means the lamp of hope has gone out.
normalIntro.cn: hopeless 意为希望之光已经熄灭。

normal.en: Without water, the situation looked hopeless.
normal.cn: 没有水，情况看起来毫无希望。

normal.en: He is hopeless at fixing things.
normal.cn: 他对修理东西一窍不通。

normal.en: She felt hopeless after the third failure.
normal.cn: 第三次失败后她感到绝望。

normal.en: It was a hopeless case from the start.
normal.cn: 这件事从一开始就无可救药。

normal.en: Do not call it hopeless while people still try.
normal.cn: 只要人们还在努力，就别说是无望的。

abstract.en: Hopeless is a judgment we often make too early.
abstract.cn: 无望，是我们常常过早作出的判断。

abstract.en: A hopeless night can still end at dawn.
abstract.cn: 再绝望的夜晚，也会在黎明结束。

abstract.en: Despair is loud, but it is not the last word.
abstract.cn: 绝望很响，但它不是最后一句。

examples.en: Without water, the situation looked hopeless.
examples.cn: 没有水，情况看起来毫无希望。

examples.en: He is hopeless at fixing things.
examples.cn: 他对修理东西一窍不通。

examples.en: She felt hopeless after the third failure.
examples.cn: 第三次失败后她感到绝望。

dict_mnemonic.text: hopeless 由 hope（希望）加 -less（没有……的）构成，表示没有希望的；口语中也可表示「对某事一窍不通」。

root: hope（希望）加后缀 -less（没有……的），表示没有任何希望的。

sensesIntro.en: Hopeless means having no hope of success, or informally very bad at something.
sensesIntro.cn: hopeless 表示没有成功的希望，口语中也可表示对某事一窍不通。

core.en: No light left in the lamp.
core.cn: 灯里再没有光。

branches.en: Without water, the situation looked hopeless.
branches.cn: 没有水，情况看起来毫无希望。

branches.en: She felt hopeless after the third failure.
branches.cn: 第三次失败后她感到绝望。

branches.en: He is hopeless at fixing things.
branches.cn: 他对修理东西一窍不通。

branches.en: A bad situation and a bad skill share the word.
branches.cn: 糟糕的局面和糟糕的技能共用一个词。

branches.en: It was a hopeless case from the start.
branches.cn: 这件事从一开始就无可救药。

intro.en: Hopeless is hope plus -less, and builds hopelessly and hopelessness.
intro.cn: hopeless 由 hope 加 -less 构成，还能派生出 hopelessly 和 hopelessness。

latinIntro.en: Hope is Germanic; -less comes from Old English leas.
latinIntro.cn: hope 属日耳曼语；-less 来自古英语 leas。

items.exampleCN: 这个案子似乎没有希望。
收容所帮助无家可归的人。

latinEntries.example: Hopian is the source of hopeless.
latinEntries.exampleCN: hopian 是 hopeless 的词源。

definition_zh: 事件；事故；（不严重的）插曲
definition_en: something that happens, especially something unusual or unpleasant, or a single small event inside a larger one
core_image: 街角的路灯下，一只打翻的牛奶瓶和一地碎玻璃被警用黄带围了起来
scene: 清晨街角的路灯下，一只牛奶瓶翻倒在地，碎玻璃散了一小片。 The police wrote down every detail of the incident before the street filled up.
sceneCN: 这里 incident 是「事件、事故」（第 1 个义项：发生的、多带负面意味的事情），句意是警察在街上人多起来之前记下了这起事件的所有细节。画面里有路灯、打翻的牛奶瓶和一小片碎玻璃。

pos.zh: 名词：事件、事故；（较大的事情中的）一件小事、插曲

collocations.phrase: at the scene of the incident

senses.title: Something that happens
senses.definition: an event, especially one that is unusual, unpleasant, or worth reporting
senses.definitionCN: 一件事情，尤指不寻常的、不愉快的或值得上报的事
senses.example: The school recorded three similar incidents last term.
senses.exampleCN: 学校上学期记录了三起类似事件。
senses.why: The word names a happening in the world, and English uses it most for things that disturb the normal order.
senses.whyCN: 这个词指世上发生的某件事，而英语最常用它来说打破常态的事情。

senses.title: A small episode inside a larger one
senses.definition: one small event that forms part of a longer story, journey, or process
senses.definitionCN: 构成一段较长经历、旅程或过程的一件小事
senses.example: The lost ticket was a minor incident in an otherwise calm journey.
senses.exampleCN: 丢车票只是这趟平顺旅程中的一个小插曲。
senses.why: Here the word orders events inside a narrative rather than warning of trouble.
senses.whyCN: 此时这个词是在叙述里给事件排位置，而不是警示有麻烦。

senses.title: An accident or clash
senses.definition: an accident, a fight, or a clash between groups, as reported by officials
senses.definitionCN: 官方通报中的意外事故、打斗或群体冲突
senses.example: A border incident nearly led to talks breaking down.
senses.exampleCN: 一起边境冲突差点让谈判破裂。
senses.why: Official language fixed the word on accidents and clashes, especially in police and military reports.
senses.whyCN: 官方语言把这个词固定在事故与冲突上，尤其在警务与军事报告中。

intro.en: Incident comes from a Latin verb for falling upon, and the idea of something that falls into your path still shapes it.
intro.cn: incident 出自拉丁语中表示「落在上面」的动词，而「落到你路上来的东西」这一意象至今仍在起作用。

items.en: Cadere meant to fall, and it underlies English words from accident to cadence and chance.
items.cn: 拉丁语 cadere 意为「落下」，accident、cadence、chance 都从它而来。

items.en: Incidere added the prefix in and meant to fall upon, as events fall upon a person.
items.cn: incidere 加前缀 in，意为「落在上面」，就像事情落在一个人身上。

items.en: The participle incidens was used as a noun for a happening, a thing that falls upon us.
items.cn: 分词 incidens 被用作名词，指落在我们身上的一件事。

items.en: French formed incident with the same sense of an event, often an unlucky one.
items.cn: 法语造出 incident，同样指一件事，且多指不走运的事。

items.en: English took it in the fifteenth century, and reporting language made it the standard word for accidents and clashes.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪借入，通报语言又把它定成事故与冲突的标准用词。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same falling root; the near-meaning group gathers other words for happenings.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「落下」词根下的词；近义组收其他表示「事情」的词。

entries.definition: An unexpected harm nobody intended, from the same Latin verb with a different prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 「意外、事故」，同一词根不同前缀，强调无人故意。

entries.definition: How often something occurs across a group or a period.
entries.definitionCN: 「发生率」，讲的是频次而不是单件事。

entries.definition: By the way; used to add a side remark.
entries.definitionCN: 副词「顺便说一下」，用来补一句旁枝的话。

entries.definition: Anything that happens, usually planned or at least neutral.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「事件」，中性，常指安排好的事情。

entries.definition: One part of a longer story or illness.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「一段插曲」，是较长故事或病程中的一节。

entries.definition: A fact of something happening, often noted in statistics.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「发生的事」，多见于统计与记录。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the falling image behind the root and the fixed phrases of official reports.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子利用词根背后「落下」的意象，以及通报中的固定搭配。

normal.en: An incident is something that falls on you; accident is the same fall with a different prefix.
normal.cn: incident 是落到你身上的事；accident 是同一种「落」，只是前缀不同。

normal.en: Without incident is the phrase for a journey that went exactly as planned.
normal.cn: without incident 形容一趟完全按计划走完的行程。

normal.en: Police write incident reports, which is why the word so often means something bad.
normal.cn: 警察写的是 incident report，所以这个词多半指不好的事。

normal.en: Incidentally means by the way, so a side event turned into a formula for changing subject.
normal.cn: incidentally 意为「顺便一提」，一件旁枝之事变成了改话题的套话。

normal.en: Keep the pair straight: an incident is one case, incidence is how often it happens.
normal.cn: 记住这一对：incident 是一件事，incidence 是发生的频率。

abstract.en: Naming something an incident is already a judgement that it is small enough to be handled.
abstract.cn: 把一件事称作 incident，本身就是在判断它小到可以处理。

abstract.en: The word carries a fall inside it, so every incident carries a hint of things going out of control.
abstract.cn: 这个词体内装着「落下」，所以每起事件都暗示着事物失去控制。

abstract.en: Reports choose the noun, and the noun sets the size: an incident rarely becomes a crisis on paper.
abstract.cn: 报告在挑选名词，名词也在设定大小：在纸上，事件很少升级为危机。

examples.en: The flight landed without incident despite the storm.
examples.cn: 尽管有暴风雨，航班还是平安落地。

examples.en: Teachers must report any incident involving a fight.
examples.cn: 任何涉及打斗的事件，教师都必须上报。

examples.en: The broken window was a small incident in an otherwise quiet term.
examples.cn: 这扇窗户被打破，只算是本该平静的一学期中的小插曲。

dict_mnemonic.text: in 在上 + cid 落 + -ent 名词词尾——落到你头上的一件事，就是事件

root: 拉丁语 incidere「落在上面」（in「在上」+ cadere「落下」）的分词 incidens 作名词，经法语 incident 于十五世纪进入英语；先泛指发生之事，后经警务与军事通报固定为「事故、冲突事件」。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: an event worth reporting, a small episode in a larger story, and an accident or clash in official language.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：值得上报的事件，长故事里的小插曲，以及官方用语中的事故与冲突。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a spilled milk bottle and a ring of glass under a street lamp in the morning.
core.cn: 核心意象：清晨路灯下，一只打翻的牛奶瓶和一圈碎玻璃。

branches.en: THE EVENT: incident names a happening that draws notice.
branches.cn: 事件线：incident 指一件引人注意的事。

branches.en: THE EPISODE: inside a story it marks one small chapter.
branches.cn: 插曲线：放在故事里，它标明一个很小的章节。

branches.en: THE REPORT: police and army language fixed it on accidents and clashes.
branches.cn: 通报线：警务与军事语言把它固定在事故与冲突上。

branches.en: THE PHRASE: without incident means all went as planned.
branches.cn: 搭配线：without incident 表示一切如常。

branches.en: THE PAIR: incidence measures how many times such events occur.
branches.cn: 对照线：incidence 量的是这类事件出现的次数。

intro.en: The table gathers words built on the Latin root cadere, to fall.
intro.cn: 此表汇集以拉丁词根 cadere「落下」为底的词。

latinIntro.en: Cadere with different prefixes produces accident, incident, occasion and decay.
latinIntro.cn: cadere 配上不同前缀，就有了 accident、incident、occasion 与 decay。

items.example: One small incident changed the mood.
Incidentally, the shop closes early today.
items.exampleCN: 顺便说一下，今天店关得早。

items.example: The incidence of the disease has doubled.
items.exampleCN: 这种病的发生率翻了一倍。

items.meaning: a particular time when something happens
items.example: It is an occasion worth remembering.
items.exampleCN: 这是个值得记住的场合。

items.meaning: to fall at the same point
items.example: The two holidays coincide this year.
items.exampleCN: 今年两个节日碰在一起。

items.example: The timbers decayed in the damp.

latinEntries.meaningCN: 拉丁语分词：落在上面，引申为发生的事

definition_zh: 解释；说明；原因
definition_en: a statement that makes something clear; a reason given for something; an account of how something works
core_image: 把复杂的东西摊开，一件件讲明白
scene: 他的解释没有消除大家的疑问。 His explanation did not remove everyone's doubt.
sceneCN: 这里 explanation 是「解释、说明」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他的解释没有消除大家的疑问。

senses.title: Statement of clarity
senses.definition: a statement that makes something clear
senses.definitionCN: 使某事变得清楚的说明
senses.example: Her explanation was easy to follow.
senses.exampleCN: 她的解释很容易理解。
senses.why: The noun names the act of making clear.
senses.whyCN: 名词形式指把事讲清楚这件事。

senses.title: Reason given
senses.definition: a reason given for something that happened
senses.definitionCN: 为已发生之事给出的原因
senses.example: There is no explanation for the delay.
senses.exampleCN: 这次延误没有任何解释。
senses.why: Making clear turns into giving a cause.
senses.whyCN: 讲清楚转化为给出原因。

senses.title: Account of how
senses.definition: an account of how something works
senses.definitionCN: 对某事物运作方式的说明
senses.example: The manual gives an explanation of each symbol.
senses.exampleCN: 手册对每个符号都作了解释。
senses.why: The reason extends to a full account.
senses.whyCN: 原因扩展到完整的说明。

intro.en: Explanation comes from Latin explanatio, a flattening out.
intro.cn: explanation 源自拉丁语 explanatio，意为「摊平、讲明」。

items.en: Planus means flat or clear.
items.cn: planus 意为平坦、清楚。

items.en: Explanare means to flatten out.
items.cn: explanare 意为把东西摊平。

items.en: Explanatio names the act of making plain.
items.cn: explanatio 指使事情明白的动作。

items.en: Explanacioun enters as a learned word.
items.cn: explanacioun 作为学术词进入英语。

items.en: Explanation covers reasons as well as clarity.
items.cn: explanation 既指清楚也指原因。

items.en: An explanation for is a common phrase.
items.cn: an explanation for 成为常用搭配。

note.en: An explanation makes things clear; an expectation is what you believe will happen.
note.cn: explanation 把事情讲清楚，expectation 则是你相信会发生的事。

entries.definition: a belief about the future
entries.definitionCN: 预期；期望

entries.definition: a careful check or a test
entries.definitionCN: 检查；考试

entries.definition: the act of traveling to learn
entries.definitionCN: 探索

entries.definition: a statement that clears confusion
entries.definitionCN: 澄清

entries.definition: a description of events
entries.definitionCN: 叙述；说明

entries.definition: a cause for something
entries.definitionCN: 原因；理由

normalIntro.en: An explanation lays the facts out so they can be seen.
normalIntro.cn: explanation 把事实摊开，让人一眼看清。

normal.en: The teacher gave a simple explanation of the rule.
normal.cn: 老师对这条规则作了简单解释。

normal.en: No explanation was offered for the missing files.
normal.cn: 文件丢失一事没有任何解释。

normal.en: His explanation convinced the whole committee.
normal.cn: 他的解释说服了整个委员会。

normal.en: The book begins with an explanation of the terms.
normal.cn: 这本书以术语解释开篇。

normal.en: She left the room without explanation.
normal.cn: 她没作解释就离开了房间。

abstract.en: Picture a tangled knot laid out straight.
abstract.cn: 想象一个乱结被摊直。

abstract.en: Imagine a teacher drawing steps on a board.
abstract.cn: 想象老师在黑板上画出步骤。

abstract.en: Think of fog clearing off a hillside.
abstract.cn: 想象山坡上的雾渐渐散开。

examples.en: The scientist offered a new explanation for the light.
examples.cn: 这位科学家对这种光提出了新解释。

examples.en: His explanation of the rules took ten minutes.
examples.cn: 他讲解规则用了十分钟。

examples.en: There is still no explanation for the accident.
examples.cn: 这起事故至今仍没有解释。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「explanation」来自 explain（解释）加 -ation：解释这个动作的结果，就是「解释、说明」。

root: 拉丁语 explanatio（摊平、说明）来自 explanare（摊平），核心义「把事情铺开讲明白」。

sensesIntro.en: Explanation means a clear statement, a reason given, or a full account of how something works.
sensesIntro.cn: explanation 意为清楚的说明、给出的原因，或对运作方式的完整阐述。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a complex thing laid out clearly.
core.cn: 核心意象：把复杂事物摊开摆清楚。

branches.en: The base sense is a clear statement.
branches.cn: 基础义是清楚的说明。

branches.en: Clarity turns into an answer about why.
branches.cn: 清楚转化为对原因的回答。

branches.en: The answer grows into a full account.
branches.cn: 回答扩展为完整的阐述。

branches.en: Clarity and cause are both offered to others.
branches.cn: 清楚与原因都是向他人交代。

branches.en: A reason and a full account often merge.
branches.cn: 原因与完整阐述常常合为一体。

intro.en: Explanation adds the noun suffix -ation to explain.
intro.cn: explanation 在 explain 后加名词后缀 -ation。

latinIntro.en: Latin explanare and explanatio supply the core forms.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 explanare 与 explanatio 提供核心词形。

items.example: Planus gives the idea of plainness.

definition_zh: 自己；自我；本性；（使）一致
definition_en: the whole being of a person, including body and mind, considered as a distinct identity
core_image: 镜子里的那个人，和你动作分毫不差
scene: 深夜卧室里，她对着穿衣镜站了很久。 She finally accepted her true self after years of doubt.
sceneCN: 这里 self 是「自我；本性」（第 2 个义项：内在的真实身份）；句意是多年怀疑之后，她终于接纳了真实的自我。

derivatives.zh: self 与 my 构成反身代词，义为「我自己」
self 与 one 构成反身代词，义为「自己」

senses.title: Your whole person as distinct from others
senses.definition: the entire person regarded apart from everyone else
senses.definitionCN: 与所有人区分开来的整个个人
senses.example: Keep the secret between your self and the diary.
senses.exampleCN: 把这个秘密留在你和日记之间。
senses.why: The mirror figure is not anyone else — it is exactly the one standing there.
senses.whyCN: 镜中人不是别人——正是站在那里的人。

senses.title: The inner identity or nature
senses.definition: the deeper identity made of feelings, beliefs, and character
senses.definitionCN: 由情感、信念与性格构成的更深层身份
senses.example: Travel helped him find his true self.
senses.exampleCN: 旅行帮他找到了真实的自我。
senses.why: The mirror shows more than the face: it shows who is behind it.
senses.whyCN: 镜子照出的不止是脸，还有脸背后的人。

senses.title: Personal interest or advantage
senses.definition: one's own benefit considered selfishly
senses.definitionCN: 从私己角度考虑的利益
senses.example: He always puts self before the team.
senses.exampleCN: 他总是把私利放在团队之前。
senses.why: The mirror figure is the only one the greedy eye serves.
senses.whyCN: 贪婪的眼睛只服务于镜中人。

senses.title: Same origin, same make, or unchanged state
senses.definition: belonging to the same origin or remaining unchanged
senses.definitionCN: 出自同一来源或保持原样
senses.example: The valley keeps its self after all the changes.
senses.exampleCN: 山谷历经变迁仍保持本色。
senses.why: The mirror never changes the figure — same face, same frame.
senses.whyCN: 镜子从不改变人影——同样的脸，同样的框。

senses.title: A combined form meaning one's own
senses.definition: a combining element meaning of oneself
senses.definitionCN: 表示「自身的」构词成分
senses.example: She checked the answer herself.
senses.exampleCN: 她亲自核对了答案。
senses.why: The mirror multiplies into every corner of the language: self-care, self-portrait.
senses.whyCN: 镜子在语言各个角落复制自己：self-care、self-portrait。

intro.en: From Old English self, one of the oldest identity words in Germanic languages.
intro.cn: 来自古英语 self，是日耳曼诸语言中最古老的「身份」词之一。

items.en: The root *selbho- likely meant own or distinct, the seed of identity words.
items.cn: 词根 *selbho- 可能意为「自己的、独特的」，是身份类词汇的种子。

items.en: Germanic languages all built their self words on this root: Dutch zelf, German selbe.
items.cn: 日耳曼诸语言的「自身」词都基于此根：荷兰语 zelf、德语 selbe。

items.en: Old English self served both as adjective (same) and noun (the person).
items.cn: 古英语 self 兼作形容词（同一的）与名词（本人）。

items.en: Reflexive compounds like myself and himself exploded in Middle English.
items.cn: myself、himself 等反身复合词在中古英语大量涌现。

items.en: Modern self anchors hundreds of compounds, from selfie to self-esteem.
items.cn: 现代 self 构成数百个复合词，从 selfie 到 self-esteem。

note.en: Look-alikes in the sel- shape, and near rivals in the identity field.
note.cn: sel- 形附近的形近词，以及「身份」义场的近义词。

entries.definition: to give goods for money
entries.definitionCN: 卖——与 self 仅差一个字母，注意拼写

entries.definition: the plural of self
entries.definitionCN: self 的复数形式，词形变化特殊

entries.definition: a board for storing things
entries.definitionCN: 架子——形近词，复数 shelves 与 selves 易混

entries.definition: who a person is
entries.definitionCN: 身份——更正式，self 更日常具体

entries.definition: the spiritual part of a person
entries.definitionCN: 灵魂——偏宗教精神层面

entries.definition: the conscious self in psychology
entries.definitionCN: 自我（心理学）——术语色彩，来自拉丁语

normalIntro.en: Hooks on the mirror picture and the irregular plural.
normalIntro.cn: 基于镜中画面与不规则复数的记忆钩子。

normal.en: self → selves: f becomes v before s, like leaf → leaves
normal.cn: self → selves：f 变 v 再加 s，规律同 leaf → leaves

normal.en: myself, yourself, himself are mirror compounds
normal.cn: myself 等反身代词就是「镜子」复合词

normal.en: selfish puts self first; selfless removes it
normal.cn: selfish 把 self 放首位，selfless 把它去掉

normal.en: by oneself means the mirror is the only company
normal.cn: by oneself 就是镜中只有自己陪伴

normal.en: selfie is the mirror turned into a phone camera
normal.cn: selfie 就是镜子变成了手机摄像头

abstract.en: Stand before the mirror and nod at the person inside
abstract.cn: 站在镜前，向镜中人点头

abstract.en: See your reflection staying still while you move
abstract.cn: 看见你移动时镜中人也纹丝不动

abstract.en: Feel the quiet moment when the mask comes off
abstract.cn: 体会面具摘下后那一刻的安静

examples.en: She looked at her aging self in the photograph.
examples.cn: 她端详着照片里日渐老去的自己。

examples.en: Meditation helped him quiet his restless self.
examples.cn: 冥想帮平息了他焦躁的内心。

examples.en: He repaired the bicycle by himself.
examples.cn: 他独自修好了自行车。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「塞尔夫」——塞尔特的自己人，自己就是自己，别想成卖东西的 sell。

root: 古英语 self「同一的、自己的」，源自日耳曼共同词根（重构形式 *selbho-，与荷兰语 zelf、德语 selbe 同源）；中古英语起与代词大量复合成反身代词，现代又催生海量 self- 复合词。

sensesIntro.en: One mirror, five reflections: the person, the inner nature, the greedy eye, the unchanging face, and the multiplying word.
sensesIntro.cn: 一面镜子，五个映像：那个人、内在本性、贪婪之眼、不变的脸与不断繁殖的词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: your own figure standing inside a mirror
core.cn: 核心意象：镜子里站着你自己的身影

branches.en: the whole figure, apart from every other
branches.cn: 与所有人分开的完整身影

branches.en: what the mirror shows behind the face
branches.cn: 脸庞背后镜子照出的东西

branches.en: the eye that serves only the reflection
branches.cn: 只服务于镜中影像的那只眼

branches.en: the face that never changes in the glass
branches.cn: 镜中那张从不改变的脸

branches.en: person and nature in one reflected frame
branches.cn: 人与本性同在一个映像框里

intro.en: English words built on self and its compound power.
intro.cn: 由 self 及其强大构词能力构成的英语词。

items.exampleCN: 他们的公开自我与私下不同。

definition_zh: 奇妙的；了不起的；惊人的；极好的；不可思议的；非凡的
definition_en: extremely good, remarkable, or surprising in a way that fills you with wonder
core_image: 掀开幕布的一瞬，台下有人倒吸一口气：眼前的东西好得不像真的
scene: 观众席安静了一秒，随即爆发出掌声。 The audience agreed that the puppet show was simply marvellous.
sceneCN: 这里 marvellous 是「绝妙的、好得令人惊叹」（第 1 个义项：质量极高、令人赞叹）；句意为观众一致认为这场木偶戏实在太精彩了；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 奇妙的；绝妙的；了不起的

derivatives.zh: 同根基础词，经古法语 merveille 进入英语，义为「奇迹；感到惊叹」
由该形容词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「精彩地；奇妙地」
由该形容词加性质名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「奇妙；非凡」
固定表达，义为「大自然的奇妙」
动词加介词构成的短语，义为「对……感到惊叹」

senses.title: Extremely good; delightful
senses.definition: so good in quality that you feel pleasure and admiration
senses.definitionCN: 质量好到让人感到愉悦与赞叹
senses.example: We spent a marvellous afternoon by the lake.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在湖边度过了一个极其愉快的下午。
senses.why: What once looked like a miracle is now applied to anything that delights you like a small wonder.
senses.whyCN: 原本指「像奇迹一样」的东西，如今泛指任何像小奇迹一样让你开心的好事。

senses.title: Remarkable; astonishing
senses.definition: so unusual or impressive that it surprises you
senses.definitionCN: 不寻常或令人印象深刻到让你吃惊
senses.example: The bridge is a marvellous feat of engineering.
senses.exampleCN: 这座桥是一项了不起的工程壮举。
senses.why: A marvel was something to be wondered at, and achievements beyond expectation keep that sense.
senses.whyCN: marvel 本指「值得惊叹之物」，超出预期的成就保留了这层含义。

senses.title: Seeming almost impossible or magical
senses.titleCN: 奇妙的；近乎不可思议的
senses.definition: appearing so strange or wonderful that it seems hardly real
senses.definitionCN: 显得奇异美妙，几乎不像真实存在
senses.example: The old clock performs a marvellous trick every hour.
senses.exampleCN: 这座老钟每小时都会上演一个奇妙的戏法。
senses.why: The root marvel named things beyond explanation, so the word still carries a faint air of magic.
senses.whyCN: 词根 marvel 本指无法解释的事物，因此这个词至今带一点魔幻气息。

senses.title: Very skilled or impressive in performance
senses.titleCN: 技艺高超的；令人叫绝的
senses.definition: said of a person, voice or skill that works so well it draws praise
senses.definitionCN: 用于形容表现好到引人称赞的人、嗓音或技能
senses.example: She has a marvellous memory for names.
senses.exampleCN: 她记名字的本领令人叫绝。
senses.why: When a human ability seems to work like a wonder, English borrows the word of wonders.
senses.whyCN: 当人的能力好得像奇迹般运转时，英语便借用「奇迹」一族的词来形容。

senses.title: Splendid in appearance or scenery
senses.titleCN: 壮丽多彩的；景色迷人的
senses.definition: strikingly beautiful, said of views, scenes or sights
senses.definitionCN: 美得出众，用于景色、场景或风光
senses.example: From the summit we admired a marvellous sunset.
senses.exampleCN: 在山顶我们欣赏了一场绝美的日落。
senses.why: Scenery that stops the viewer is treated as a wonder shown to the eyes.
senses.whyCN: 让观看者驻足的景色，被当作呈现在眼前的「奇观」。

senses.title: Delightfully amusing or entertaining
senses.definition: amusing or entertaining in a way that gives great pleasure
senses.definitionCN: 有趣好笑，带来极大乐趣
senses.example: He told a marvellous story about his first job.
senses.exampleCN: 他讲了一个关于自己第一份工作的妙趣横生的故事。
senses.why: Pleasure and laughter are close cousins of delight, so good fun also earns the word of wonders.
senses.whyCN: 乐趣与欢笑同「愉悦」是近亲，所以精彩好笑的事也配得上「奇迹」一族的词。

senses.title: Convenient or wonderfully useful
senses.definition: said of a tool, device or arrangement that works remarkably well for you
senses.definitionCN: 用于形容对你来说好用得出奇的工具、装置或安排
senses.example: This little gadget is marvellous for opening jars.
senses.exampleCN: 这个小玩意儿开罐头好用极了。
senses.why: When an object solves a problem almost too well, it is praised as if it were a small miracle.
senses.whyCN: 当一件东西好用到近乎不可思议时，人们便像称赞小奇迹一样称赞它。

senses.title: Said in emphatic agreement or praise
senses.definition: used as an exclamation of strong approval
senses.definitionCN: 用作表示强烈赞许的感叹词
senses.example: Marvellous! The plan is settled, then.
senses.exampleCN: 太好了！那计划就这么定了。
senses.why: Words of wonder easily become cries of joy, so the adjective stands alone in speech.
senses.whyCN: 表惊叹的词很容易变成欢呼，于是这个形容词在口语中可独立成句。

intro.en: Marvellous comes, through Old French merveilleux, from Vulgar Latin *mirabilia 'wonderful things', the plural of Latin mirabilis 'wonderful', from mirari 'to wonder at'. English adopted it in the thirteenth century, and it shares the root with marvel and miracle.
intro.cn: marvellous 经古法语 merveilleux，源自通俗拉丁语 *mirabilia「奇妙之物」，即拉丁 mirabilis「奇妙的」的复数，词根为 mirari「感到惊异」；英语在十三世纪采用，与 marvel、miracle 同根。

items.en: The root *smei is generally reconstructed as meaning 'to smile, to laugh', and wonder was felt as something that makes you open up in delight; this reconstruction is not fully certain.
items.cn: 一般认为印欧词根 *smei 意为「微笑、笑」，惊叹被感受为令人开颜之物；此重构形式并非定论。

items.en: Mirari meant 'to wonder at', mirabilis meant 'wonderful', and its plural *mirabilia named 'wonderful things'.
items.cn: 拉丁 mirari 意为「对……感到惊异」，mirabilis 意为「奇妙的」，其复数 *mirabilia 指「奇妙之物」。

items.en: The word became merveille 'a wonder' and merveilleux 'wonderful', passing into English as marvel and marvellous.
items.cn: 古法语变为 merveille「奇迹」与 merveilleux「奇妙的」，进入英语后成为 marvel 与 marvellous。

items.en: English marvellous first described wonders and strange sights in romance and religious writing, then widened to strong praise of anything excellent.
items.cn: 英语的 marvellous 起初在传奇与宗教文学中形容奇观异事，后扩大为对一切出色事物的强烈赞美。

items.en: British spelling keeps the double l as marvellous, while American spelling simplifies it to marvelous; both come from the same source.
items.cn: 英式拼写保留双写 l 作 marvellous，美式拼写简化为 marvelous；两者同源。

items.en: Today the word mainly means 'extremely good', and its old sense of 'strange, full of wonder' survives in literary style.
items.cn: 如今这个词主要表示「极好的」，旧的「奇异、充满惊叹」之义保留在文学语体中。

note.en: The first group shares the wonder root mirari; the second group holds praise words that differ in strength and flavour.
note.cn: 第一组共享「惊叹」词根 mirari；第二组是表示赞美的词，在强度与色彩上各有不同。

entries.definition: A wonderful thing, or the act of feeling great surprise; the base word of the family.
entries.definitionCN: 令人惊叹的事物，或感到大为惊异；是同族词的基础词。

entries.definition: The American spelling of marvellous, with one l and the same meaning.
entries.definitionCN: marvellous 的美式拼写，只有一个 l，意义相同。

entries.definition: An event believed to be caused by divine power; from Latin mirabilis via Old French.
entries.definitionCN: 被认为由神力造成的奇迹；经古法语源自拉丁 mirabilis。

entries.definition: Very good or amazing; the most general praise word of the family.
entries.definitionCN: 极好的或令人惊叹的；同族中最通用的赞美词。

entries.definition: Impressive and beautiful; it stresses brilliance rather than wonder.
entries.definitionCN: 出色的、华美的；强调光彩夺目而非惊叹。

entries.definition: Informal for extremely good; originally about fables and legends.
entries.definitionCN: 口语中指「极好的」；原义与寓言、传说相关。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real derivatives and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实派生词与真实固定搭配，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The root is Latin mirari 'to wonder at', shared by marvel, miracle and miraculous.
normal.cn: 词根是拉丁 mirari「感到惊异」，与 marvel、miracle、miraculous 同根。

normal.en: The word came through French merveilleux, so the v and the ending -ous both show French shape.
normal.cn: 此词经法语 merveilleux 传入，所以其中的 v 与词尾 -ous 都是法语印记。

normal.en: The family runs marvel, marvellous, marvellously, marvellousness.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 marvel（奇迹）、marvellous（奇妙的）、marvellously（奇妙地）、marvellousness（奇妙）。

normal.en: British spelling doubles the l; American spelling writes marvelous with one l.
normal.cn: 英式拼写双写 l，美式拼写写作 marvelous，只有一个 l。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark praise: a marvellous opportunity, marvellous news, a marvellous view.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出赞美用法：绝好的机会、极好的消息、奇妙的景色。

abstract.en: Picture a curtain rising on something so good that the whole hall gasps.
abstract.cn: 想象幕布升起，眼前的精彩让全场倒吸一口气。

abstract.en: Picture a traveller telling of sights so strange that listeners marvel rather than doubt.
abstract.cn: 想象旅人讲述奇景，听者只顾惊叹，来不及怀疑。

abstract.en: Picture a small gadget that solves in one click what took an hour before.
abstract.cn: 想象一个小工具，一键解决了从前要花一小时的事。

examples.en: The guide showed us a marvellous hidden valley behind the ridge.
examples.cn: 向导带我们看了山脊后一条奇妙的隐秘山谷。

examples.en: She has done marvellous work with the children's reading club.
examples.cn: 她把孩子们的读书会办得非常出色。

examples.en: It is marvellous that the old bridge survived the flood.
examples.cn: 那座老桥能在洪水中幸存，真是不可思议。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「马窝乐死」——这匹马住进窝棚舒服得乐死了，好得不像话

root: 拉丁 mirari「感到惊异」→ mirabilis「奇妙的」→ 通俗拉丁 *mirabilia「奇妙之物」→ 古法语 merveilleux → 英语 marvellous；同族 marvel、miracle、miraculous。印欧词根 *smei（微笑）为重构形式，存疑。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all grow from one image of wonder: delight in quality, astonishment at achievement, an almost magical strangeness, superb skill, splendid scenery, delightful fun, wonderful usefulness, and a cry of approval.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都从「惊叹」这一个意象生长：对品质的欣喜、对成就的惊叹、近乎魔幻的奇异、高超的技艺、壮丽的景色、妙趣的欢乐、好用得出奇，以及一声赞叹。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a curtain rises, and what appears is so good or so strange that viewers can only marvel.
core.cn: 核心意象：幕布升起，眼前的景象好得或奇得让人只能惊叹。

branches.en: THE DELIGHT FORM: things so pleasant that you feel joy rather than mere approval.
branches.cn: 愉悦形态：让人心生欢喜而不仅是认可的事物。

branches.en: THE ACHIEVEMENT FORM: works and skills so impressive that they astonish.
branches.cn: 成就形态：令人惊叹的出色成果与技艺。

branches.en: THE STRANGENESS FORM: things so odd and lovely that they seem unreal.
branches.cn: 奇异形态：奇异美妙到近乎不真实的事物。

branches.en: THE OBJECT FORM: splendid views and wonderfully useful things.
branches.cn: 对象形态：壮丽的景色与好用得出奇的东西。

branches.en: THE SPOKEN FORM: the word alone, as a cry of strong approval.
branches.cn: 口语形态：单词独立成句，化作一声赞叹。

intro.en: Marvellous rests on Latin mirari 'to wonder at' and the French-derived ending -ous; English adds endings for manner, state and the verb of wondering.
intro.cn: marvellous 建立在拉丁 mirari「感到惊异」与源自法语的词尾 -ous 之上；英语再加表示方式、状态与惊叹动作的词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin mirari 'to wonder at' gives the family: mirabilis 'wonderful', *mirabilia 'wonderful things', and through French the noun marvel and the adjective marvellous.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 mirari「感到惊异」孕育整个词族：mirabilis「奇妙的」、*mirabilia「奇妙之物」，经法语得到名词 marvel 与形容词 marvellous。

items.meaning: to wonder at; to be astonished
items.example: The verb is the root of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是整个词族的根源。

items.example: The adjective also gave English miracle via French.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词经法语也给出英语 miracle。

items.meaning: full of; having the quality of
items.example: The ending turns the noun marvel into a describing word.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把名词 marvel 变成描述词。

items.example: The noun passed into English as marvel.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词进入英语后成为 marvel。

items.example: This is the direct source of the English adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这是英语形容词的直接来源。

items.meaning: a wonder; to feel great surprise
items.example: The noun and verb kept the older, stronger sense.
items.exampleCN: 名词与动词保留了更古老更强的义项。

items.example: The suffix gives the degree adverb marvellously.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀给出程度副词 marvellously。

items.example: The suffix names the state of being wonderful.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀命名「奇妙」的状态。

items.example: The adverb modifies verbs of performing and working.
items.exampleCN: 这个副词修饰「表现」「起作用」类动词。

items.example: The noun appears in literary description.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词出现在文学描写中。

definition_zh: 矿物；矿物质；（营养）无机盐
definition_en: a naturally occurring inorganic solid with a definite chemical composition and structure, and by extension such substances in nutrition
core_image: 一块带晶面的矿石放在木托盘上，旁边一小堆白色晶体盐
scene: 地质课上，老师把一块深色矿石样本传给学生看。 The sample was a dark mineral with a metallic lustre, harder than glass.
sceneCN: 这里 mineral 指「矿物」（第 1 个义项：天然产出的无机固体，有确定成分与结构）；它呈深色、带金属光泽，硬度超过玻璃。图中可辨识物件：矿石标本、晶面、木托盘、硬度测试片；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 矿物；矿物质；（复数）无机养分、矿质元素
矿物的；含矿物的（如 mineral water、mineral resources）

senses.title: A natural inorganic solid
senses.titleCN: 矿物：天然产出的无机固体
senses.definition: a naturally formed inorganic solid with a definite chemical composition and a characteristic crystal structure
senses.definitionCN: 天然形成的无机固体，具有确定的化学成分与特征晶体结构
senses.example: Quartz is a mineral made of silicon and oxygen.
senses.exampleCN: 石英是由硅与氧构成的矿物。
senses.why: Geology defines minerals by four tests at once: natural, inorganic, definite composition, ordered structure.
senses.whyCN: 地质学同时用四条标准界定矿物：天然、无机、成分确定、结构有序。

senses.title: Dietary minerals
senses.titleCN: 矿物质养分：人体必需的无机元素
senses.definition: in nutrition, the inorganic elements such as calcium, iron and zinc that the body needs in small amounts
senses.definitionCN: 营养学中指钙、铁、锌等人体少量必需的无机元素
senses.example: Leafy greens supply calcium and other minerals.
senses.exampleCN: 绿叶蔬菜提供钙与其他矿物质。
senses.why: Nutrition borrowed the geology word because these nutrients arrive as mineral salts rather than as carbon compounds.
senses.whyCN: 营养学借用地质学词汇，因为这些养分以矿物盐而非碳化合物的形式到来。

senses.title: Mineral water and springs
senses.titleCN: 矿泉水：含溶解矿物质的天然水
senses.definition: water drawn from a spring and containing dissolved mineral salts, often sold as a drink
senses.definitionCN: 取自泉水、含溶解矿物盐的水，常作为饮品出售
senses.example: The hotel serves local mineral water from the valley spring.
senses.exampleCN: 旅馆供应来自山谷泉眼的当地矿泉水。
senses.why: The adjective simply says what the water contains, and the phrase mineral water then became a product category.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词只是说明水含有什么，而「矿泉水」这一短语随后成了一个产品类别。

senses.title: Mineral resources and rights
senses.titleCN: 矿产资源与矿权：法律经济意义上的矿物
senses.definition: in law and economics, the valuable inorganic substances in the ground and the rights to extract them
senses.definitionCN: 法律与经济中指地下有价值的无机物质及开采它的权利
senses.example: The state owns all mineral rights beneath private land.
senses.exampleCN: 私有土地之下的一切矿权归国家所有。
senses.why: Because extraction is worth money, the word shifts from a scientific category to a legal asset.
senses.whyCN: 由于开采具有经济价值，这个词从科学分类转成了法律资产。

senses.title: Rock-forming minerals
senses.titleCN: 造岩矿物：组成岩石的基本单元
senses.definition: in petrology, the individual mineral species whose grains make up a rock
senses.definitionCN: 岩石学中指构成岩石颗粒的各个矿物种类
senses.example: Granite is a rock made of quartz, feldspar and mica minerals.
senses.exampleCN: 花岗岩是由石英、长石与云母等矿物构成的岩石。
senses.why: Petrologists must name the parts as well as the whole, so mineral is the countable unit inside an uncountable rock.
senses.whyCN: 岩石学家既要命名整体也要命名部件，因此 mineral 是岩石这个不可数整体中的可数单元。

senses.title: Ore minerals
senses.titleCN: 矿石矿物：值得开采提炼的矿物
senses.definition: the mineral in a deposit that contains a metal or other element valuable enough to extract
senses.definitionCN: 矿床中含金属或其他元素、值得提炼的矿物
senses.example: Chalcopyrite is the main ore mineral of copper.
senses.exampleCN: 黄铜矿是铜的主要矿石矿物。
senses.why: Mining distinguishes the valuable grains from the worthless gangue, so ore mineral is a commercial as well as a geological label.
senses.whyCN: 采矿把有价值的颗粒与无价值的脉石分开，因此矿石矿物既是地质标签也是商业标签。

senses.title: The mineral kingdom
senses.titleCN: 矿物界：旧自然分类中的第三界
senses.definition: in older natural history, the third division of the natural world beside the animal and vegetable kingdoms
senses.definitionCN: 旧自然史中指与动物界、植物界并列的自然界第三界
senses.example: Old textbooks divided nature into animal, vegetable and mineral kingdoms.
senses.exampleCN: 旧教科书把自然分为动物界、植物界与矿物界。
senses.why: Before modern chemistry, classifying by kingdom was the easiest way to place lifeless matter.
senses.whyCN: 在现代化学之前，按「界」分类是把无生命物质归位的最简便方法。

senses.title: Specimens and gems
senses.titleCN: 矿物标本与宝石：收藏与鉴赏对象
senses.definition: a cut or collected mineral specimen valued for colour, crystal form or rarity
senses.definitionCN: 因颜色、晶形或稀有性而被切磨或收藏的矿物标本
senses.example: The museum displays minerals from old copper mines.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆展出旧铜矿出产的矿物标本。
senses.why: Collectors treat the same scientific object as an aesthetic one, so the word also names what sits in a display case.
senses.whyCN: 收藏者把同一个科学对象当作审美对象，因此这个词也指展柜里的东西。

intro.en: Mineral comes from Medieval Latin minerale, from minera 'ore, mine'. The deeper origin of minera is disputed and may be Celtic.
intro.cn: mineral 出自中世纪拉丁 minerale，源自 minera「矿石、矿」。minera 的更深来源有争议，可能来自凯尔特语。

items.en: Medieval Latin minera meant 'ore, mine, pit'. It appears in mining and metallurgical texts from the late Middle Ages.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁 minera 意为「矿石、矿、矿坑」，见于中世纪末的采矿与冶金文献。

items.en: Many etymologists link minera to a Celtic root for ore, seen in Welsh mwyn 'ore'. This link is generally accepted but not proved.
items.cn: 许多词源学家把 minera 与表示矿石的凯尔特词根联系起来，可见威尔士语 mwyn「矿石」。这一联系被普遍接受，但未经证实。

items.en: Others derive it from Latin minari 'to jut, to project', because ore bodies stand out from the rock. This explanation is less favoured.
items.cn: 另有人把它追溯到拉丁 minari「突出、伸出」，因为矿体在岩石中显眼。这一解释较少被采纳。

items.en: Old French mineral passed into English in the late Middle Ages, first as an adjective for substances dug from the earth.
items.cn: 古法语 mineral 在中世纪末进入英语，最初作形容词，指从地下挖出的物质。

items.en: Chemistry fixed the modern geological definition in the nineteenth century, and nutrition later borrowed the word for dietary elements.
items.cn: 化学在 19 世纪确立了现代地质学定义，营养学后来又借这个词指膳食元素。

items.en: Source uncertainty: the origin of minera is unresolved; both the Celtic and the Latin minari explanations are hypotheses, and the first English date is uncertain.
items.cn: 来源不确定：minera 的来源尚无定论；凯尔特说与拉丁 minari 说都属假说，英语首见年代亦存疑。

note.en: The first group holds words built on mineral that name studies or processes rather than the substance; the second holds earth materials that are often called minerals loosely.
note.cn: 第一组是由 mineral 构成、却指学科或过程的词；第二组是常被宽泛称作矿物的地球材料。

entries.definition: The scientific study of minerals, their composition, structure and classification. It is a discipline, not a substance.
entries.definitionCN: 研究矿物的成分、结构与分类的学科。它是一门学问，不是物质。

entries.definition: To convert organic matter into mineral form, or to impregnate something with minerals.
entries.definitionCN: 把有机物转化为矿物形态，或用矿物浸染某物。

entries.definition: Describes something that has been converted into or impregnated with mineral matter, such as mineralized bone.
entries.definitionCN: 描述已被转化为矿物或被矿物浸染的事物，如矿化骨。

entries.definition: A natural aggregate of one or more minerals. A rock is the whole mixture; a mineral is one ingredient.
entries.definitionCN: 由一种或多种矿物组成的天然集合体。岩石是整体混合物，矿物是其中一种成分。

entries.definition: A solid whose atoms are arranged in a repeating pattern. Many minerals form crystals, but glass is a solid without that order.
entries.definitionCN: 原子呈重复排列的固体。许多矿物形成晶体，但玻璃是缺乏这种有序性的固体。

entries.definition: Rock or mineral material rich enough in a metal to be mined at a profit. All ore contains minerals, but most minerals are not ore.
entries.definitionCN: 金属含量高到值得开采获利的岩石或矿物材料。矿石都含矿物，但多数矿物并非矿石。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: minera 'ore' + -ale: what comes out of a mine.
normal.cn: minera「矿石」+ -ale：从矿里出来的东西。

normal.en: The family runs mineralize, mineralization, mineralogy, mineralogist and mineralogical.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 mineralize、mineralization、mineralogy、mineralogist、mineralogical。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the fields: mineral water, mineral resources, mineral deposit, essential minerals.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：矿泉水、矿产资源、矿床、必需矿物质。

normal.en: A rock is a mixture; a mineral is one ingredient with a fixed formula.
normal.cn: 岩石是混合物；矿物是成分固定的一种配料。

normal.en: Nutrition calls calcium and iron minerals because they arrive as inorganic salts.
normal.cn: 营养学把钙与铁称为矿物质，因为它们以无机盐形式到来。

abstract.en: Picture a cut stone with flat shiny faces lying on a wooden tray.
abstract.cn: 想象一块切开的石头，平面闪亮，躺在木托盘上。

abstract.en: Picture a glass of still water with a faint mineral taste and a spring behind it.
abstract.cn: 想象一杯静水，带一点矿物味，背后是一眼泉。

abstract.en: Picture an old chart dividing the world into animal, vegetable and mineral bands.
abstract.cn: 想象一张旧图把世界分成动物、植物与矿物三条带。

examples.en: The region is rich in mineral deposits but short of water.
examples.cn: 该地区矿产丰富，却缺水。

examples.en: Iron is a mineral that many people do not get enough of.
examples.cn: 铁是许多人摄入不足的一种矿物质。

examples.en: The geologist identified the green mineral as malachite.
examples.cn: 地质学家把那块绿色矿物鉴定为孔雀石。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「mine（矿）+ ral」——从矿里挖出来的东西 → mineral 矿物

root: 中世纪拉丁 minera「矿石、矿」→ minerale → 古法语 mineral → 英语 mineral。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one substance from a crystal in rock to a nutrient in food, a product on a shelf, a legal right, an ore, an old kingdom and a museum specimen.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项让同一种物质从岩石中的晶体走到食物里的养分、货架上的产品、法律上的权利、矿石、旧时的「界」与博物馆标本。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a faceted stone on a tray beside a heap of white salt crystals.
core.cn: 核心意象：木托盘上的晶面矿石，旁边一小堆白色盐晶。

branches.en: GEOLOGY: the definition needs nature, no life, a fixed formula and an ordered structure.
branches.cn: 地质：定义需要天然、无生命、成分固定与结构有序四条。

branches.en: NUTRITION: the same word names the inorganic elements the body needs.
branches.cn: 营养：同一个词指身体所需的无机元素。

branches.en: PRODUCT: dissolved salts turn spring water into a branded drink.
branches.cn: 产品：溶解的盐把泉水变成有品牌的饮品。

branches.en: VALUE: rights underground and ore in the vein both measure the word in money.
branches.cn: 价值：地下的权利与矿脉中的矿石，都用钱来衡量这个词。

branches.en: CLASSIFICATION AND BEAUTY: an old kingdom and a display case are two ends of the same label.
branches.cn: 分类与美：旧时的「界」与展柜，是同一标签的两端。

intro.en: Mineral is a Medieval Latin noun ending in -ale, the suffix that turns a stem into a thing name, later used as an adjective without change.
intro.cn: mineral 是带 -ale 的中世纪拉丁名词，该后缀把词干变成事物名，后来它又原形用作形容词。

latinIntro.en: Medieval Latin minera supplied the stem and minerale the noun; the -alis ending later produced English mineralogy through a different path.
latinIntro.cn: 中世纪拉丁 minera 提供词干、minerale 提供名词；-alis 词尾后来经另一条路径产生了英语 mineralogy。

items.meaning: a natural inorganic solid; also an adjective
items.meaningCN: 天然无机固体；也作形容词
items.example: The mineral is harder than steel.
Soil microbes mineralize the organic matter.
items.exampleCN: 土壤微生物把有机质矿化。
矿化作用保存了这具化石。
矿物学按对称性给晶体分类。
矿物学家鉴定了这块标本。

items.example: The mineralogical survey mapped the district.
items.exampleCN: 矿物学调查绘制了该区地图。

items.meaning: to remove minerals from water or bone
items.meaningCN: 从水或骨中去除矿物质
items.example: The filter demineralizes the tap water.
items.exampleCN: 该过滤器去除自来水中的矿物质。

items.meaning: a person who works in a mine
items.example: The miners went down at dawn.
